eva: Quick heads-up — trying to onboard llama3-13b-quant to dedicated. Weights are at s3://redwood-models/llama3/13b/quant-v1/model.pt and model.yaml is in the same bucket. Running a quick tokenization smoke shows an extra <BOS> token in the tokenizer vocab. Our chat templates assume no explicit BOS. Anyone seen this pattern before?

matt: @eva good catch. Some of the Llama variants include a special bos_token_id=1 in the tokenizer.json. Do you have the tokenizer file path?

eva: s3://redwood-models/llama3/13b/quant-v1/tokenizer.json — quick diff vs the standard llm-base tokenizers:
```
-   "bos_token": null
+   "bos_token": "<s>",
    "eos_token": "</s>",
    "unk_token": "<unk>"
```
So model returns a BOS when encoding. Our chat template prepends system prompt + user, so we'll end up with double BOS in the kv cache.

cleo: double BOS can shift token indexes for prefix caching. For inference we can either strip the model's BOS or adjust our prompt builder to accept explicit bos. Which is easier for Dedicated rollout?

ravi: For rollout speed, strip BOS at encode time in the request pipeline. Add a flag in model-config: `strip_bos: true` so existing apps don't change. But we should add a test to ensure we don't accidentally remove a semantic BOS for models that require it.

eva: good plan. I'm prepping a patch. Draft model-config snippet: 
```yaml
model: llama3-13b-quant-v1
weights: s3://redwood-models/llama3/13b/quant-v1/model.pt
tokenizer: s3://redwood-models/llama3/13b/quant-v1/tokenizer.json
strip_bos: true
expected_bos_token: "<s>"
```
Will run `redwood model validate` before pushing.

samir: heads-up: CI's tokenizer-compat test will fail if we change behavior. Add a unit that encodes a canonical chat turn and asserts length matches baseline after strip. Example test: `tests/test_tokenizer_compat.py::test_llama3_strip_bos`. Also ping @matt for code review.

matt: @samir @eva please add the test and a short migration note in the model catalog. I'll review the PR today. Also add an entry to the rollout playbook about kv-cache rekeying — we had a cache mismatch in a previous deploy.

eva: added TODOs in the PR description. Quick question: do we prefer to implement stripping in the tokenizer adapter (fast) or in the request-normalizer middleware (centralized)?

cleo: tokenizer adapter is lower-risk and keeps request pipeline unchanged. But middleware makes it observable at runtime (metrics). Maybe both: adapter strips and middleware emits a metric if strip_bos=true.

ravi: agree with cleo. Adapter change + metric is a good pattern. Also update `redwood model validate` to check tokenizer.json has expected tokens when strip_bos is set: if expected_bos_token missing -> fail.

eva: will add validation. One more quirk: chat template expects messages to be joined with `\n### Assistant:` etc. But this model's tokenizer splits `###` into separate tokens weirdly, bloating token counts. Any quick mitigation?

samir: two options: use a different delimiter (e.g., `\n\nAssistant:`) or add a post-tokenize compacting step that merges frequent token sequences. For now, prefer changing templates to `\n\nAssistant:` for this model only and flag it in model.yaml as `chat_delimiter: "\n\nAssistant:"`.

matt: make sure to benchmark token count delta. If it's +5% cost we should consider a quant tweak instead. Also include the change in Optimize recommendations.

eva: noted. I'll run a tokenization sample of 1000 typical prompts and post results.

ci-bot: build/llama3-onboard #78 started by eva — running unit tests (includes tokenizer-compat).

deploy-bot: staging deploy scheduled for next Tue (canary) — mark if PR merges before 23:59 UTC Mon.

cleo: small reminder: update the dev-examples snippet for chat templates. People copy-paste that one a lot.

eva: quick sample of the encoder check I'm using:
```py
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
t = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json')
ids = t.encode('Hello').ids
print(ids[:5])  # ensure first id != bos_id if strip_bos
```
I'll add this to tests.

samir: @eva when you post the CI results, tag me if it fails — I can flip the test harness to run locally.

eva: thanks — pushing PR now. Will follow up with perf numbers and the PR link. :rocket:

matt: :eyes: thanks everyone. If anyone sees token misalignment in canary, open an urgent thread in #incidents.

eva: PR URL: https://git.redwood.ai/p/redwood/models/+/1234 (adding tests + strip_bos + chat_delimiter change). CI currently running.
